stories.headline: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru's Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
stories.title: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru's Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
stories.summary: Lima, Nov 21: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake shook the Andes in central Peru on Friday with no immediate reports of damage or casualties. The US Geological Survey said the earthquake struck at 7:09 pm local time (0900 GMT Saturday). Its epicentre was in the Andes, 34 kilometres (21 miles) north of Junin, at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles). Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets. Peru lies along the "Ring of Fire", a 40,000-kilometre (25,000-mile) arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the world's earthquakes occur. In August, a 6.7 magnitude earthquake in the Peruvian Andes left two people injured and damaged several homes, health centres and schools, while in July, a 5.5-magnitude quake in the Junín region resulted in six deaths and 30 injuries.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan disrupts air traffic, 14 flights cancelled in Ranchi
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan disrupts air traffic, 14 flights cancelled in Ranchi
stories.summary: As many as 14 flights were cancelled at the Birsa Munda Airport in Ranchi on Saturday due to inclement weather triggered by cyclone 'Akvan', an official said. Jharkhand has been experiencing cloudy weather coupled with light rain since Friday under the influence of the cyclone. For safe landing or take-off, a visibility between 1,200 and 1,500 metres is required. "The visibility at Ranchi airport was around 1,000 metres until 1pm," Airport Director Vinod Kumar told PTI. He said that 14 scheduled flights were cancelled due to bad weather.

stories.headline: Heavy rain lashes Odisha as Cyclone Akvan weakens, flood alert continues
stories.title: Heavy rain lashes Odisha as Cyclone Akvan weakens, flood alert continues
stories.summary: Heavy rain lashes Odisha as Cyclone Akvan weakens, flood alert continues
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Officials have been directed to remain alert and continue precautionary measures as persistent rain has raised water levels in most rivers.

The Odisha government has put the water resources department on high alert and ordered round-the-clock surveillance of rivers and reservoirs after Cyclone Akvan weakened following heavy rain across the state, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
However, the water resources department said the state's major rivers remained below warning and danger levels.
The depression left by Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan moved northwards over south coastal Odisha and weakened into a distinct low-pressure area on Friday, the Meteorological Centre in Bhubaneswar said.
It was expected to continue moving northwards over Odisha and weaken further within six hours.
Manorama Mohanty, director of the Meteorological Centre, said rainfall had reduced significantly, though some districts were expected to continue receiving rain.
These included Balasore, Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, Jagatsinghpur, Jajpur, Puri, Khurda and Cuttack.
"Very heavy rain is likely at some places, although several areas have already received substantial rainfall," Mohanty said.
Sources in the water resources department told PTI that Balasore and Cuttack districts had received average rainfall of about 50 mm by 8.30 am on Saturday.
Bhograi in Balasore recorded the highest rainfall at 143 mm, followed by Odogaon in Nayagarh at 108 mm, Buguda in Ganjam at 102 mm and Tangi-Choudwar in Cuttack at 90 mm.
The India Meteorological Department said one place in the state had received very heavy rainfall and 13 places had recorded heavy rainfall during the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Saturday.
Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the Odisha government was in touch with the water resources department secretary because rain was also possible in Jharkhand.

stories.headline: Srikakulam releases 15,440 cusecs as inflows moderate after cyclone floods
stories.title: Srikakulam releases 15,440 cusecs as inflows moderate after cyclone floods
stories.summary: The district administration heaved a sigh of relief as inflows are moderate compared to inflows of nearly one lakh cusecs one month ago due to the cyclone that caused havoc in Ichchapuram and other places
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: As many as 15,440 cusecs of water from the Bahuda River were discharged downstream on Saturday (November 21, 2026) morning as inflows continued from upstream, which witnessed heavy rains for the last few days with the impact of the Akvan cyclone.

The district administration heaved a sigh of relief as inflows are moderate compared to inflows of nearly one lakh cusecs one month ago due to the cyclone that caused havoc in Ichchapuram and other places.
Irrigation officials released 3,600 cusecs from the Gotta barrage of Vamasadhara, and 3,100 cusecs of Nagavali water were discharged from Narayanpur Anicut.
Srikakulam collector Swapnil Dinakar Pundkar said that the situation was under control in spite temporary inundation of crops in Ichchapuram and other places.
He said that agriculture officials will visit the fields and give necessary suggestions to farmers.

stories.headline: Remnants of Cyclone Akvan to bring rain in Bengal till November 22: IMD
stories.title: Remnants of Cyclone Akvan to bring rain in Bengal till November 22: IMD
stories.summary: According to the IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by gusty winds reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph are likely over most districts of south Bengal and a few places in north Bengal on Saturday
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The remnants of severe cyclonic storm Akvan, which weakened into a low-pressure area on Saturday (November 21, 2026), will bring rain to West Bengal till November 22 morning, the IMD said.
The storm moved towards West Bengal after making landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha on Friday (November 20) morning, bringing heavy rain to south Bengal since November 19 evening.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by gusty winds reaching speeds of 30-40 kmph are likely over most districts of south Bengal and a few places in north Bengal on Saturday (November 21).
Mainly dry weather is likely to prevail across the state from November 24, with minimum temperatures expected to fall by two to three degrees Celsius, the Met department said.

With the weakening storm bringing very heavy rain over the coastal districts, the seaside tourist town of Digha in Purba Medinipur district recorded the State's highest rainfall at 176 mm in 24 hours till 8.30 a.m., according to the IMD data.
Kanthi in the same district received 105 mm rainfall during the period, while Sagar island in the other coastal district of South 24 Parganas district received 85 mm rain, it said.
Kolkata received 41 mm of rain during the same period as the Met forecast a cloudy sky with light to moderate rain for the city on Saturday (November 21).

stories.headline: CONMEBOL backs Infantino re-election bid with ‘strong support’
stories.title: CONMEBOL backs Infantino re-election bid with ‘strong support’
stories.summary: Infantino faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he also retains support from Africa and Asia for his bid to win re-election next March.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'world cup' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has “unanimous” backing for reelection as head of world football from CONMEBOL, the ten-country South American bloc said Friday.
Infantino faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he also retains support from Africa and Asia for his bid to win re-election next March.
Each country has one vote with 211 members and the winner will need to secure at least 106 votes in the ballot scheduled for March 18 in Rabat.
Conmebol has 10, Africa has 54 and Asia 46.
The CONMEBOL statement was made at Barranquilla ahead of Saturday’s Copa Sudamericana final between Brazil’s Atletico Mineiro and Argentina’s Boca Juniors.
CONMEBOL said it appreciated “the leadership of the current FIFA president” and the “positive transformations in football” that he has driven since taking office in 2016.
Having been the sole candidate in 2019 and 2023, Infantino faces two declared challengers: Frenchman Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima.

Infantino has fended off criticism of the enlargement of the World Cup, giving a FIFA Peace Prize to Donald Trump and -- at the American president’s request -- overturning a red card for a US player during the competition.
Infantino is under severe pressure for the first time, but mainly due to UEFA’s reaction to the private investor plan that forced his humiliating climbdown.
UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has given full backing to Diallo, while Tashima has pledged to restore “integrity” to world football’s governing body.
Tashima, who serves on the FIFA Council, stressed his intention to restore trust in the governing body and make transparency and integrity the hallmarks of his campaign.
He said he decided to run after he was incensed by FIFA’s shock decision to lift the ban on United States player Folarin Balogun.

stories.headline: India says no change in its position on IWT as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
stories.title: India says no change in its position on IWT as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 20: India's position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) is "very clear" and there has been "absolutely no change" in it, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Friday, amid a visit by Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi. Malik, who arrived here in the early hours of Friday, attended the opening day of the three-day forum in the evening. The event, being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. India had announced on October 28 that invitations had been extended to all SCO members, including Pakistan, in keeping with established practice. It was perhaps the first time New Delhi had invited a Pakistani minister to attend an event in India since the May 7-10 military hostilities last year following Operation Sindoor. Pakistan had announced on November 14 that its Climate Change Minister Malik would participate in the forum. At his bi-weekly media briefing, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked how New Delhi viewed Malik's participation in the India-hosted forum, given that he does not hold the culture portfolio and had reportedly made comments on the IWT. "As far as IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear, and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Jaiswal said. India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives. Malik's participation in the forum is being seen by some experts as an opportunity in a multilateral framework that may help improve ties between the two neighbours. Interacting with reporters on the sidelines of the forum, Malik, when asked about the role of culture in fostering better ties between India and Pakistan, said, "Culture has a very key role to play". Hours before the inauguration, the MEA on Friday said the forum was a "multilateral event within the SCO framework", for which invitations had been extended to all members of the grouping, including Pakistan. "India is hosting the 1st SCO Civilisation Dialogue on 20-22 November 2026, in New Delhi. This is a multilateral event within the SCO framework, for which invitations have been extended to all members of the SCO, including Pakistan," the MEA said in a post on X. "Observers and Dialogue Partners of the SCO have also been invited to attend the Dialogue, which will be inaugurated this evening by the Hon’ble Prime Minister," it said. The event is being hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the MEA. The SCO was founded at a summit in Shanghai in 2001 by the presidents of Russia, China, the Kyrgyz Republic, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. India and Pakistan became its permanent members in 2017.

stories.headline: NRI Talk | NRIs are moving beyond deposits to mutual funds and global investing; Belong manages $20 million in AUM: Ankur Choudhary
stories.title: NRI Talk | NRIs are moving beyond deposits to mutual funds and global investing; Belong manages $20 million in AUM: Ankur Choudhary
stories.summary: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are increasingly looking beyond traditional bank deposits to explore mutual funds, global equities and other investment opportunities, signalling a shift from simply parking overseas savings to actively building and diversifying wealth. The trend is also creating opportunities for financial platforms operating out of GIFT City, which aim to make cross-border investing more accessible through foreign-currency products and digital onboarding.Belong, a GIFT City-based savings and investment platform for NRIs, has crossed $20 million in assets under management (AUM) within about a year of its launch in August 2025, with investors from more than 20 countries. While USD fixed deposits and FCNR deposits continue to account for a significant share of its assets, the platform is seeing growing interest in GIFT City mutual funds and global investment products, including US stocks and ETFs.In an interview with Kshitij Anand of ETMarkets, Ankur Choudhary, Co-founder of Belong, discusses how NRI investment preferences are evolving, why GIFT City is gaining traction as a cross-border investment hub, the role of currency diversification and tax efficiency, and what could unlock the next phase of NRI participation. Edited Excerpts –Q) Are NRIs moving from traditional deposits and remittances towards active wealth creation and portfolio diversification?A) Yes. Active NRI demat accounts in India tripled from about 3.15 lakh in FY19 to over 9.5 lakh by July 2026, and the value of NRI equity holdings rose from about ₹1.5 lakh crore to ₹5.6 lakh crore over the same period.In GIFT City, NRI accounts at banks went from about 3,700 in March 2024 to about 20,000 in March 2026, and over 30,000 by June, according to IFSCA. Deposits grew from $600 million to $1.96 billion. Investors in GIFT City retail fund schemes went from 255 in September 2025 to 8,467 in June 2026.We see the same pattern on Belong. New NRI investors are more curious about investment products like mutual funds. NRIs who started with USD fixed deposits go on to add GIFT City mutual funds and other investment products.You can also hear it in the questions NRIs ask. A few years ago the main question was which deposit to park their surplus money in. Now they ask about global investing and tax efficiency on the potential returns.136048387Q) Is India becoming a more attractive investment destination for NRIs compared with traditional financial centres?A) Yes, India remains a core allocation for a large section of NRIs even though its markets have lagged recently due to the AI trade. This is especially true for those in Southeast Asia and in the Middle East, home to more than half of all NRIs.The war in the Middle East also led many NRIs there to move money to India and GIFT City in search of safety. GIFT City has also improved access by allowing NRIs to invest in India with tax-efficient structures and in US dollars, directly from their foreign bank accounts.Onshore regulators have made positive moves too. In June 2026, the limit on how much of a listed company an individual NRI or OCI can own was raised from 5% to 10%, and the combined limit for NRIs and OCIs from 10% to 24%. SEBI has also allowed NRIs and OCIs in FATF-compliant countries to complete KYC remotely for onshore investing from 3 December.Q) What does the IFSC framework offer NRIs compared with conventional routes?A) Compared with the conventional India investing route via NRE/NRO accounts, the IFSC framework provides significant benefits and ease of access. The first is currency - banks, fund management entities and other financial institutions operating within the IFSC can provide products to NRIs in multiple foreign currencies, including but not limited to US Dollars.So an NRI can now avail Dollar or Euro banking from an Indian bank itself. Similarly, mutual funds based in GIFT City IFSC typically accept investments in USD and publish their NAVs in USD as well. There are also no investment or repatriation limits for NRIs.The second is ease of access - NRIs need NRE/NRO accounts in India in order to invest in Indian mutual funds. Opening and maintaining an NRE/NRO account from abroad has usually been challenging for NRIs, especially those who don’t visit India frequently.The IFSC framework completely does away with such a requirement. NRIs can invest in IFSC based mutual funds and other capital market products from their foreign bank accounts itself. There is no need to open an NRE/NRO account in India, even a bank account in IFSC is not needed.Coupled with digital KYC for NRIs brought in with IFSCA in 2025, it makes accessing IFSC based products much easier for NRIs. The third is freedom from India side taxation - An NRI selling an Indian equity fund typically faces 12.5% to 20% TDS on gains.Tax in the NRI's country of residence also applies. Certain countries have beneficial DTAA arrangements with India which lesser the tax burden but availing them requires annual Indian tax filing and submitting tax residence certificates and multiple other paperwork.The IFSC framework does away with India side taxation for most products for NRIs e.g. interest on GIFT City bank deposits and capital gains on GIFT City based India focused funds are tax-free in India for non-residents with no TDS or ITR filing required.Q) FCNR(B) deposits revived sharply after the RBI's special window in 2026. Was it rates, or rupee weakness?A) Rupee weakness triggered the RBI to open the window. Rates started the revival and leverage gave it scale. When the window opened in June, the RBI covered the hedging cost on fresh three-to-fiveyear deposits and lifted the rate ceiling. USD FCNR(B) rates went from around 3% to 6-7% at many banks. That was the trigger.The scale came from leverage. Banks, including GIFT City banking units, lent NRIs huge sums of dollars to place in these deposits, almost doubling or tripling the returns. At Belong, we facilitated over $50 Mn in leveraged FCNR deposits for our customers with our partner banks.Q) How should NRIs approach currency diversification? Is investing in India necessarily the best way to deploy overseas savings?A) The right approach is always diversification across countries and asset classes because no single market or asset class performs well at all times. The last two years illustrate this. Indian equities have lagged global markets with AI exposure, and rupee weakness was significant enough this year to prompt the RBI’s special FCNR(B) window.GIFT City makes it easier for NRIs to achieve this diversification of investing both in India and globally from one place. opening: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are increasingly looking beyond traditional bank deposits to explore mutual funds, global equities and other investment opportunities, signalling a shift from simply parking overseas savings to actively building and diversifying wealth.

The trend is also creating opportunities for financial platforms operating out of GIFT City, which aim to make cross-border investing more accessible through foreign-currency products and digital onboarding.
body: Belong, a GIFT City-based savings and investment platform for NRIs, has crossed $20 million in assets under management (AUM) within about a year of its launch in August 2025, with investors from more than 20 countries.

While USD fixed deposits and FCNR deposits continue to account for a significant share of its assets, the platform is seeing growing interest in GIFT City mutual funds and global investment products, including US stocks and ETFs.

In an interview with Kshitij Anand of ETMarkets, Ankur Choudhary, Co-founder of Belong, discusses how NRI investment preferences are evolving, why GIFT City is gaining traction as a cross-border investment hub, the role of currency diversification and tax efficiency, and what could unlock the next phase of NRI participation.
Edited Excerpts –Q) Are NRIs moving from traditional deposits and remittances towards active wealth creation and portfolio diversification?
A) Yes.

Active NRI demat accounts in India tripled from about 3.15 lakh in FY19 to over 9.5 lakh by July 2026, and the value of NRI equity holdings rose from about ₹1.5 lakh crore to ₹5.6 lakh crore over the same period.
In GIFT City, NRI accounts at banks went from about 3,700 in March 2024 to about 20,000 in March 2026, and over 30,000 by June, according to IFSCA.
Deposits grew from $600 million to $1.96 billion.
Investors in GIFT City retail fund schemes went from 255 in September 2025 to 8,467 in June 2026.
We see the same pattern on Belong.
New NRI investors are more curious about investment products like mutual funds.
NRIs who started with USD fixed deposits go on to add GIFT City mutual funds and other investment products.
You can also hear it in the questions NRIs ask.
A few years ago the main question was which deposit to park their surplus money in.
Now they ask about global investing and tax efficiency on the potential returns.
Q) Is India becoming a more attractive investment destination for NRIs compared with traditional financial centres?
A) Yes, India remains a core allocation for a large section of NRIs even though its markets have lagged recently due to the AI trade.
This is especially true for those in Southeast Asia and in the Middle East, home to more than half of all NRIs.
The war in the Middle East also led many NRIs there to move money to India and GIFT City in search of safety.
GIFT City has also improved access by allowing NRIs to invest in India with tax-efficient structures and in US dollars, directly from their foreign bank accounts.
Onshore regulators have made positive moves too.
In June 2026, the limit on how much of a listed company an individual NRI or OCI can own was raised from 5% to 10%, and the combined limit for NRIs and OCIs from 10% to 24%.
SEBI has also allowed NRIs and OCIs in FATF-compliant countries to complete KYC remotely for onshore investing from 3 December.
Q) What does the IFSC framework offer NRIs compared with conventional routes?
A) Compared with the conventional India investing route via NRE/NRO accounts, the IFSC framework provides significant benefits and ease of access.

The first is currency - banks, fund management entities and other financial institutions operating within the IFSC can provide products to NRIs in multiple foreign currencies, including but not limited to US Dollars.
So an NRI can now avail Dollar or Euro banking from an Indian bank itself.
Similarly, mutual funds based in GIFT City IFSC typically accept investments in USD and publish their NAVs in USD as well.
There are also no investment or repatriation limits for NRIs.
The second is ease of access - NRIs need NRE/NRO accounts in India in order to invest in Indian mutual funds.
Opening and maintaining an NRE/NRO account from abroad has usually been challenging for NRIs, especially those who don’t visit India frequently.
The IFSC framework completely does away with such a requirement.
NRIs can invest in IFSC based mutual funds and other capital market products from their foreign bank accounts itself.
There is no need to open an NRE/NRO account in India, even a bank account in IFSC is not needed.
Coupled with digital KYC for NRIs brought in with IFSCA in 2025, it makes accessing IFSC based products much easier for NRIs.
The third is freedom from India side taxation - An NRI selling an Indian equity fund typically faces 12.5% to 20% TDS on gains.
Tax in the NRI's country of residence also applies.

Certain countries have beneficial DTAA arrangements with India which lesser the tax burden but availing them requires annual Indian tax filing and submitting tax residence certificates and multiple other paperwork.

The IFSC framework does away with India side taxation for most products for NRIs e.g. interest on GIFT City bank deposits and capital gains on GIFT City based India focused funds are tax-free in India for non-residents with no TDS or ITR filing required.
Q) FCNR(B) deposits revived sharply after the RBI's special window in 2026.
Was it rates, or rupee weakness?
A) Rupee weakness triggered the RBI to open the window.
Rates started the revival and leverage gave it scale.
When the window opened in June, the RBI covered the hedging cost on fresh three-to-fiveyear deposits and lifted the rate ceiling.
USD FCNR(B) rates went from around 3% to 6-7% at many banks.
That was the trigger.
The scale came from leverage.
Banks, including GIFT City banking units, lent NRIs huge sums of dollars to place in these deposits, almost doubling or tripling the returns.
At Belong, we facilitated over $50 Mn in leveraged FCNR deposits for our customers with our partner banks.
Q) How should NRIs approach currency diversification?
Is investing in India necessarily the best way to deploy overseas savings?
A) The right approach is always diversification across countries and asset classes because no single market or asset class performs well at all times.
The last two years illustrate this.
Indian equities have lagged global markets with AI exposure, and rupee weakness was significant enough this year to prompt the RBI’s special FCNR(B) window.
GIFT City makes it easier for NRIs to achieve this diversification of investing both in India and globally from one place.
Within GIFT City, an NRI can hold multi-currency deposits, invest in funds focused on India or global markets, and trade US stocks and ETFs, free from any India taxation or currency restrictions.
Beyond geographical diversification, investment decisions should also account for crossborder tax considerations and liquidity needs, and NRIs may consult a financial adviser on these.
Q) What needs to change for fintech platforms to become meaningful alternatives to traditional banks?
A) Fintechs have already replaced traditional banks when it comes to wealth management.
In India, the top 3 stock brokers are all non-bank sponsored brokers.
However when it comes to core banking activities - accounts, deposits, cards and lending - banks are still miles ahead of any fintech in India.
Here banks win on trust induced by brand, regulatory backing and physical presence.

Fintechs can still compete on easier digital experience and more customer focused products but for them to become meaningful alternatives, they need to be welcomed into the regulatory infrastructure as well.
On the part of the fintechs, there has to be a corresponding commitment to being regulated - something that we have followed at Belong from day one.
Q) What regulatory changes from IFSCA could make GIFT City more competitive and unlock the next phase of NRI investments?
A) IFSCA has been quite proactive and already the existing regulations cover more ground than the currently available products in GIFT City.
So in a sense, the industry is lagging behind the regulator.
However, there are some changes that can unlock real growth for NRIs in GIFT City.

The primary change is regarding onboarding for non-residents - under IFSCA’s current regulations, video KYC is only allowed for NRIs and not for OCIs and foreign nationals and is dependent on Aadhaar.
Expanding the scope of video KYC and removing the Aadhaar dependency would increase the participation multi-fold.

Dual listing of Indian stocks/derivatives on GIFT City exchanges - While GIFT City has enabled the MF route for non-residents to invest in India, access to Indian stocks is still only available onshore via NRE/NRO and PIS/non PIS demat accounts which can be quite cumbersome for non-residents.
A mirror listing of Indian stocks on GIFT City exchanges for non-residents can bring in demand sitting on the sidelines due to friction.
Even some tax related aspects can be further streamlined to make GIFT City a place for global investing for NRIs.

Today, GIFT City funds that invest globally and pool money from both resident Indians and non-residents are taxed at the fund level at the highest marginal rates irrespective of who the end investor is.
A segregation or pass through of tax liability whereby non-residents don't get taxed for global investing via GIFT City will go a long way in making GIFT City a truly global investing platform.
Q) Belong has reportedly been growing at around 20% month-on-month.
What is driving this, and how much comes from the UAE compared with other markets?
A) Several factors have contributed to our continued growth and reaching a milestone of $20 Mn in AUM in just about a year of launch.
The war in the middle east also resulted in NRIs moving money from there to India and GIFT City looking for safety.
Then came RBI’s FCNR push which further drove rates higher and attracted deposits from NRIs.
75% of our AUM today is across USD FDs and FCNR (excluding leverage).
On the mutual fund side, our growth has primarily been on the back of increasing product range in GIFT City.
The first retail mutual fund in GIFT City was launched in September 2025 and now there are close to 15 such funds in GIFT City investing in India and globally available on Belong.
While we have investors from over 20 countries, the UAE is our largest market, at about twothirds of investors and 70% of AUM coming from there.
Q) Which products or services are likely to become the biggest revenue contributors for Belong?
A) Currently the majority of the revenue comes from GIFT City USD FDs and mutual funds.
However, as a GIFT City based broker we have recently launched some trading products as well - GIFT Nifty Futures and US stocks and ETFs.
We will soon be launching US options as well.

Initial response has been good and we believe brokerage income from these products can be the major revenue drivers in the coming years, especially as more exchange traded products get listed in GIFT City.
The regulator has recently cleared the deck for listing for foreign ETFs and allowing commodity trading on GIFT City exchanges.
Q) Please tell us more about the cross-border wealth platform?
A) Belong is a global cross-border wealth platform built from GIFT City, India’s international financial services centre.
It enables NRIs to invest both in India and globally from one place.
NRIs can invest directly from their foreign bank accounts, without opening an NRE or NRO account in India, and complete their KYC digitally.
The platform offers USD fixed deposits with GIFT City banks, GIFT City mutual funds investing in India and globally, GIFT Nifty futures, and US stocks and ETFs, with US options to follow.
Belong provides these products as a GIFT City regulated broker and distributor.

stories.title: India GDP growth projected at 7% for FY27
stories.summary: India’s real GDP growth is projected at about 7 per cent in FY27, Brickwork Ratings said, citing public capital expenditure, domestic demand and services, while forecasting a December 2026 repo rate hike amid inflation pressures.

article_sentences: India’s real GDP growth is projected at about 7 per cent in FY27, Brickwork Ratings said, citing public capital expenditure, domestic demand and services, while forecasting a December 2026 repo rate hike amid inflation pressures.

Mumbai: India’s real GDP growth is projected at approximately 7 per cent for FY27, supported by sustained public capital expenditure, resilient domestic demand and strong services activity, according to a new Brickwork Ratings (BWR) report released on Saturday.

However, persistent inflationary pressures are expected to keep monetary policy tight, with BWR anticipating a further 25-basis-point (bps) repo rate hike in December 2026, taking the policy rate to 5.75 per cent, followed by an extended pause.
“India’s growth momentum is increasingly being supported by the strength of its domestic economy and the resilience of its services exports.
However, the external environment remains an important variable, particularly given India’s dependence on energy and other key imports,” said Rajeev Sharan, Head of Research, Brickwork Ratings.

In the current environment, businesses with healthy balance sheets, adequate liquidity and the ability to manage input-cost volatility will be better positioned to navigate uncertainty, the report said.
For the broader economy, sustaining investment momentum while strengthening external resilience will remain important, Sharan said.
Government capital expenditure reached Rs 6.55 lakh crore in the first half of FY27, supporting infrastructure investment, the report said.
Services activity remained robust, with the Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rising to 55.8 in October and the Composite PMI reaching 56.2.
Industrial production grew 6.7 per cent in September, while manufacturing output expanded 7.6 per cent.
October Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections also rose 22.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2.31 lakh crore, reflecting festive demand and higher import-related collections.
Capital goods and electrical equipment, automobiles, IT services and export-oriented sectors are relatively better positioned, the report said.

stories.headline: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
stories.title: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has set aside a Calcutta High Court judgment that reduced an arbitral award in favour of a dredging contractor by 50%, holding that a court exercising jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, cannot interfere with an award merely because the amount granted for additional work appears excessive.

The Court held that the High Court's conclusion that the claim for additional work, which exceeded 70% of the original contract value, shocked its conscience was not a legally sustainable ground for modifying the award.

A bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran set aside a Calcutta High Court Division Bench order that had reduced the arbitral award by 50% on the ground that the amount awarded for additional work exceeded the original contract value by over 70%.

The Court noted that since the additional amount arose from repeated dredging undertaken by the contractor to keep the channel and basin operational, thus, the High Court had mechanically exercised its jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to set aside the award on the mere ground that it exceeded the contract work value merely noting that it shocked the court's conscience without providing a “substantive reason which blatantly and patently brings forth the conflict with the most basic notions of morality or justice, resulting in the conscience of the Court being shocked.”

“…the impugned order has merely used the words on the sole ground of the bills for the additional work having exceeded 70% of the original contract; without looking at the nature of the additional work involved… The Division Bench considering the application under Section 37 has not looked into the measurement or the invoices, which in any event, would be an exercise of adjudication on merits, clearly prohibited under the Act of 1996.
The measurements and invoices raised are of one character, based on the additional work of redredging which cannot be compartmentalised as 'valid' and 'invalid'.”, the Court said.

The dispute arose from a contract awarded by the Kolkata Port Trust to Marino Dredgeco for dredging the riverbed and shores at Sagar Island to create an approach channel and basin for a pilot station.
During execution, repeated dredging became necessary due to siltation, adverse weather conditions, and differences between the actual soil conditions and the data supplied by the Port Trust.
The Port Trust also entrusted additional work through a letter dated July 19, 2000.
After completing the work, the contractor raised additional bills, which led to arbitration.
The Arbitrator awarded the claimed amounts, and the Single Judge upheld the award under Section 34.

However, the High Court Division Bench, in an appeal under Section 37, reduced the amount by 50% and reduced interest, reasoning that the additional-work claims exceeded 70% of the original contract value and shocked the Court's conscience, following which an appeal was filed by the award holder, Marino Dredgeco, before the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks Centre for response on bringing in law on marriages between those closely related by blood
stories.summary: Counsel for the petitioner highlighted the need to create awareness about the inter-generational consequences of such marriage
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court asked the government for a response to a plea to bring a law to regulate consanguineous marriages.
A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana noted that the court cannot regulate such ‘consanguineous marriages’.
The issue fell exclusively within the domain of the legislature, the court said.
Counsel for the petitioner highlighted the need to create awareness about the inter-generational consequences of such marriage.

“We are issuing notice for the limited purpose of impressing upon the Union of India to consider the desirability of bringing a suitable legislation, or to ensure wide publicity through different channels, including a proper curriculum,” the Bench said.
The court said it could intervene on the question of sensitisation, more than issue directions.
The petitioner’s counsel said safeguards should be provided as the practice of consanguineous marriages was increasing.

stories.headline: INS Sahyadri reaches Vietnam to strengthen naval partnership
stories.title: INS Sahyadri reaches Vietnam to strengthen naval partnership
stories.summary: Hanoi, Nov 21: In a move to boost maritime cooperation between India and Vietnam, the Indian Naval Ship (INS) Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city of the Southeast Asian nation for an operational turnaround. In a post on X on Saturday, the Indian Embassy in Vietnam posted: "The ship was accorded a warm welcome by the Vietnam People's Navy and local authorities. The visit reaffirms our shared commitment to peace, stability and security in the region and in the Indo-Pacific." INS Sahyadri arrived at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang city on Friday for a three-day goodwill visit aimed at deepening defence ties and strengthening naval cooperation between India and Vietnam, local media reported. The Indian Navy frigate was accorded a warm welcome by local authorities, the city's armed forces and the Naval Region 3 Command. The Indian Naval ship, with 294 officers and sailors aboard, will remain in Da Nang until November 22 as part of its goodwill visit, Vietnamese newspaper SGGP reported. As part of the engagements, the Indian Navy delegation will meet the leadership of the Da Nang City People's Committee and the Naval Region 3 Command. The two navies will also participate in sports exchanges involving their officers and personnel. The crew will additionally explore the city's historical and cultural attractions. The visit is expected to promote greater mutual understanding and trust between the two naval forces and deepen defence cooperation between the two countries. Earlier this month, a four-member delegation of the Vietnam People's Army visited the College of Military Engineering (CME) in Pune, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme. The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions. "Strengthening India-Vietnam Defence Cooperation. A four-member delegation of the Vietnam People's Army visited the College of Military Engineering (#CME), Pune, from 03 to 05 November 2026, as part of the Subject Matter Expert Exchange (SMEE) programme," the Indian Army posted on X. "The visit focused on sharing expertise in combat engineering, counter-IED operations, HADR and engineering support to UN Peacekeeping Missions. The engagement further strengthened professional ties, mutual understanding and bilateral military cooperation between India and Vietnam," it added. Recently, National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval was on an official visit to Vietnam, where he called on Vietnamese President To Lam and thanked him for his 'steadfast support in strengthening the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership'. ( IANS)

The crew will additionally explore the city's historical and cultural attractions.

stories.headline: Maharashtra sees worst drought since 1972, Rabi sowing falls
stories.title: Maharashtra sees worst drought since 1972, Rabi sowing falls
stories.summary: Mumbai, Nov 21 : Maharashtra is facing one of its worst droughts in recent history, with Rabi sowing falling well below levels recorded during the devastating 1972 drought. According to the state Agriculture Department, only 14.74 lakh hectares have been sown so far in the 2026-27 Rabi season, compared with 47.29 lakh hectares during the 1972-73 season, raising fears that this could become the lowest Rabi sowing season on record in the state. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) and global weather organisations have declared the active El Niño in the Pacific Ocean to be a powerful "Super El Niño." Its direct impact on the monsoon led to a 19 per cent rainfall deficit across Maharashtra compared to the average, with Solapur recording the sharpest drop at 59 per cent below normal. Almost every district received deficient rainfall, and whatever rain did fall occurred largely within a 15-day window in July. Consequently, the Kharif season failed, and acute drinking water shortages in rural areas have slowed Rabi sowing to a crawl. The state Agriculture Department holds Rabi sowing records dating back to 1960. While Maharashtra's average Rabi sowing area is 55 to 60 lakh hectares, the historical comparison underscores the severity of the current crisis. "During the 1972-73 Rabi season, sowing for food grains was done on 36,64,000 hectares against 7,79,812 hectares this year, pulses 4,31,000 hectares against 6,78,385 hectares and oil seeds 6,34,000 hectares against paltry 16,106 hectares. Against the total sowing area of 47,29,000 hectares in 1972-73, only 14,74,304 hectares are there across the state in 2026-27," added the agriculture department. Previously, the lowest Rabi sowing in the state's history was recorded in 1991–92 at 40 lakh hectares. Experts see virtually no possibility of this year's total crossing the 20 to 25 lakh hectare mark by the end of December. "Farmers in the state are genuinely facing a severe drought situation. The Agriculture Department has appealed to farmers to cultivate fodder crops using whatever water is available for irrigation. Providing food grains to people is manageable, but supplying fodder and water for livestock is a massive challenge. The government and the Agriculture Department are planning meticulously to tackle the impending crisis," said the state Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharane. The drought has visibly disrupted rural life and impacted the Kartiki Yatra, a major pilgrimage of the Warkari sect. Anticipating a turnout of 12 to 15 lakh devotees, the local administration had made extensive arrangements in Pandharpur. However, only a little over 3 lakh devotees arrived in the temple town by Friday. The official Mahapuja was performed on Saturday by Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. Earlier, the Maharashtra Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav-Patil on November 19 announced that the state government has included six additional talukas in its list of drought-affected regions, taking the total number of drought-hit talukas in the state for the Kharif 2026 season to 310. The newly added talukas are Dindori (Nashik district), Wada and Vikramgad (Palghar district), Chiplun (Ratnagiri district), and Hatkanangale and Gadhinglaj (Kolhapur district). A Government Resolution (GR) formalising the decision has been issued. The state had earlier declared 304 talukas drought-affected based on rainfall deficit and other parameters during the 2026 Kharif season. Following representations seeking the inclusion of remaining affected areas, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis directed the administration during a recent Cabinet meeting to conduct a 20 per cent sample survey of five major crops and carry out on-ground field verification in accordance with Central government norms. Based on subsequent reports submitted by the respective District Collectors, these six talukas were added to the list, Minister Jadhav-Patil said. With this notification, a comprehensive package of drought relief measures and concessions has come into effect across the newly included talukas. Minister Jadhav-Patil said the government has provided exemptions in land revenue, restructuring of crop loans, and a stay on the recovery of agriculture-related loans. While agricultural pumps up to 7.5 horsepower (HP) already enjoy a full power bill waiver, pumps exceeding 7.5 HP in these talukas will receive concessions on current electricity bills. Furthermore, power connections to agricultural pumps in scarcity-declared villages will not be disconnected. ( IANS)
